"""Complete external gate receipts; expected diagnostics remain visible."""
import json
import fcntl
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from common import BASE, canonical, need, pin


if __name__ == '__main__':
    need(len(sys.argv)>=3, 'named check and explicit command')
    name,command=sys.argv[1],sys.argv[2:]
    path=BASE/'checks.json'
    lock_path=Path('.artifacts/observer-regex-values-20261010/checks.lock')
    lock_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
    with lock_path.open('a+b') as lock:
        fcntl.flock(lock,fcntl.LOCK_EX)
        saved=json.loads(path.read_bytes()) if path.exists() else {}
        need(name not in saved, 'retain first complete check result')
    inputs={str(p):pin(p.read_bytes()) for p in sorted(BASE.glob('*.py'))}
    inputs.update({arg:pin(Path(arg).read_bytes()) for arg in command if Path(arg).is_file()})
    result=subprocess.run(command,capture_output=True,text=True)
    # Commands may run independently; only this short read/merge/write is
    # serialized. Reload after the child so an older invocation cannot erase
    # a receipt completed while it was running.
    with lock_path.open('a+b') as lock:
        fcntl.flock(lock,fcntl.LOCK_EX)
        saved=json.loads(path.read_bytes()) if path.exists() else {}
        need(name not in saved, 'retain first complete check result')
        saved[name]=dict(command=command,status=result.returncode,stdout=result.stdout,stderr=result.stderr,inputs=inputs)
        path.write_bytes(canonical(saved))
    print(name,result.returncode,result.stdout[-1400:],result.stderr[-1800:],flush=True)
    need(type(result.returncode) is int and result.returncode==0,'external check success: '+name)

"""Select complete authored regex recipes before current native observation."""
import re
from common import AUTHORITY, BASE, CENSUS, SCALAR, SCOPE, canonical, module, need, pin, read, save


def source():
    return module(SCALAR/'derive.py')['source']()


def recipes(authority):
    catalogue = authority['source_recipes']
    test = catalogue['source_units']['test']['body']
    result = []
    for helper in catalogue['callbacks']:
        statement, declaration = helper['source_statement'], helper['source_declaration']
        need(statement in test and (declaration is None or declaration in test), 'whole authored source statement/declaration custody')
        location = declaration or statement
        expressions = list(re.finditer(r'qr/([^/\n]*)/([A-Za-z]*)', location))
        need(len(expressions) == 1, 'one complete finite authored regex expression')
        match = expressions[0]
        body, flags = match.groups()
        need(re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_ .'*-]+", body) is not None and flags == '',
             'finite authored ASCII pattern alphabet and absent modifiers')
        need(helper['pattern'] == '(?^:'+body+')', 'source literal versus inherited pattern evidence')
        result.append(dict(helper=helper['index'], statement=statement, declaration=declaration,
            expression=match.group(), body=body, authored_modifiers=flags, source_encoding='ASCII characters',
            original_native_flags_encoding='not measured', label=helper['label'], subtest=helper['subtest'],
            api_members=helper['api_members'], parse_members=helper['parse_members']))
    return result


def collect(authority, census, model):
    authored = recipes(authority)
    by_helper = {r['helper']:r for r in authored}
    need(len(by_helper) == len(authored), 'distinct whole authored helper allocation')
    members = []
    for row in census['operands']:
        if row['schema'] != 'regex_source':
            continue
        path = row['path']
        need(path[:1] == ['modes'] and path[2] == 'cases' and path[4] == 'phases', 'complete regex case/phase path')
        case = model['modes'][path[1]]['cases'][path[3]]
        recipe = by_helper[case['helper']]
        need(case['index'] in recipe['api_members' if case['domain']=='api' else 'parse_members']
             and case['subtest'] == recipe['subtest'], 'whole authored helper case/subtest allocation')
        operand = row['input']
        need(operand == dict(kind='regex_source', role='source_refusal_pattern', source_pattern='(?^:'+recipe['body']+')',
             display_body=recipe['body']), 'whole source regex operand body/role/schema')
        members.append(dict(path=path, helper=case['helper'], mode=model['modes'][path[1]]['mode'],
            domain=case['domain'], index=case['index'], phase=path[5], operand=operand))
    return dict(scope=SCOPE, authored=authored, members=members)


def token(body, flags, limit):
    complete = limit < 3 or len(body) <= limit
    prefix = body if complete else body[:limit-3]
    return dict(token='qr('+prefix+')'+('' if complete else '...')+flags, prefix=prefix, complete=complete)


def plan(product):
    bodies = sorted({r['body'] for r in product['authored']})
    cases = []
    for body in bodies:
        for constructor in ('literal', 'byte-string', 'upgraded-string'):
            flags = 'u' if constructor == 'upgraded-string' else ''
            for limit in (16, 64, 0):
                cases.append(dict(id=pin(canonical([body,constructor,limit]))['sha256'], body=body,
                    expression='qr/'+body+'/', constructor=constructor, modifiers=flags,
                    pattern_utf8=constructor=='upgraded-string', limit=limit, display=token(body,flags,limit)))
    return dict(scope=SCOPE, profile=dict(MaxArgNums=0, MaxEvalLen=0, RefArgFormatter=None), cases=cases)


def main():
    model = source()
    product = collect(read(AUTHORITY), read(CENSUS/'census.json'), model)
    save('regexes.json',product)
    save('plan.json',plan(product))
    need(not (BASE/'native.json').exists(), 'source hypotheses before native observation')
    save('pre-observation.json',dict(native_present=False, scope=SCOPE,
        inputs={str(p):pin(p.read_bytes()) for p in [AUTHORITY, CENSUS/'census.json', CENSUS/'source-models.json',
            *sorted(BASE.glob('*.py')), BASE/'native.pl', BASE/'regexes.json', BASE/'plan.json']}))
    print('PASS whole authored expressions, source allocations and finite public regex hypotheses before native observation.')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

"""Independent literal parsing, source traversal and whole public trace oracle."""
import json
from common import BASE, SCOPE, canonical, need, pin, same


def authored(authority):
    catalogue = authority['source_recipes']
    body = catalogue['source_units']['test']['body']
    result = []
    for helper in catalogue['callbacks']:
        statement, declaration = helper['source_statement'], helper['source_declaration']
        need(statement in body and (declaration is None or declaration in body), 'independent whole authored source custody')
        text = statement if declaration is None else declaration
        need(text.count('qr/') == 1, 'independent unique authored qr expression')
        start = text.index('qr/')
        stop = text.index('/', start+3)
        pattern = text[start+3:stop]
        end = stop+1
        while end < len(text) and text[end].isalpha():
            end += 1
        modifiers = text[stop+1:end]
        alphabet = set("abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789_ .'*-")
        need(pattern and set(pattern) <= alphabet and not modifiers,
             'independent whole ASCII pattern/absent authored modifiers')
        need(helper['pattern'] == '(?^:'+pattern+')', 'independent source versus dated pattern meaning')
        result.append(dict(helper=helper['index'], statement=statement, declaration=declaration,
            expression=text[start:end], body=pattern, authored_modifiers=modifiers, source_encoding='ASCII characters',
            original_native_flags_encoding='not measured', label=helper['label'], subtest=helper['subtest'],
            api_members=helper['api_members'], parse_members=helper['parse_members']))
    return result


def members(model, recipes):
    result = []
    pending = [(model['modes'], ['modes'])]
    helpers = {r['helper']:r for r in recipes}
    while pending:
        value, path = pending.pop()
        if type(value) is list:
            pending.extend((value[i], path+[i]) for i in reversed(range(len(value))))
        elif type(value) is dict:
            if value.get('kind') == 'regex_source':
                need(set(value) == {'kind','role','source_pattern','display_body'} and value['role']=='source_refusal_pattern',
                     'independent closed source regex schema/role')
                mode, case = model['modes'][path[1]], model['modes'][path[1]]['cases'][path[3]]
                recipe = helpers[case['helper']]
                need(case['index'] in recipe['api_members' if case['domain']=='api' else 'parse_members']
                     and case['subtest']==recipe['subtest'], 'independent entire helper/source case allocation')
                need(value['source_pattern']=='(?^:'+recipe['body']+')' and value['display_body']==recipe['body'],
                     'independent complete source regex body')
                result.append(dict(path=path,helper=case['helper'],mode=mode['mode'],domain=case['domain'],
                    index=case['index'],phase=path[5],operand=value))
            pending.extend((value[k],path+[k]) for k in sorted(value,reverse=True))
    return result


def selected(recipes):
    result = []
    patterns = set(r['body'] for r in recipes)
    for body in sorted(patterns):
        for constructor in ['literal','byte-string','upgraded-string']:
            unicode = constructor == 'upgraded-string'
            flags = 'u' if unicode else ''
            for length in [16,64,0]:
                complete = length <= 2 or len(body) <= length
                visible = body if complete else ''.join(body[i] for i in range(length-3))
                spelling = ''.join(['qr(',visible,')','' if complete else '...',flags])
                result.append(dict(id=pin(canonical([body,constructor,length]))['sha256'],body=body,
                    expression='qr/'+body+'/',constructor=constructor,modifiers=flags,pattern_utf8=unicode,limit=length,
                    display=dict(token=spelling,prefix=visible,complete=complete)))
    return result


def source(authority,model,product,plan):
    need(set(product)=={'scope','authored','members'} and set(plan)=={'scope','profile','cases'}, 'closed complete regex products')
    need(product['scope']==plan['scope']==SCOPE,'original versus current regex scope')
    recipes = authored(authority)
    need(same(recipes,product['authored']),'whole independent authored regex expressions/flags/encoding')
    allocation = members(model,recipes)
    need(same(allocation,product['members']),'complete independent regex member/order/role/schema allocation')
    need(same(plan['profile'],dict(MaxArgNums=0,MaxEvalLen=0,RefArgFormatter=None)),'selected complete public profile')
    cases = selected(recipes)
    need(same(cases,plan['cases']),'whole independent regex constructor/value/flags/encoding/display hypotheses')
    return dict(authored=pin(canonical(recipes)),members=pin(canonical(allocation)),cases=pin(canonical(cases)),scope=SCOPE)


def native(plan,receipt,driver):
    need(set(receipt)=={'command','status','stdout','stderr','inputs'},'closed complete public regex receipt')
    need(type(receipt['status']) is int and receipt['status']==0 and receipt['stderr']=='','actual typed public regex success')
    observed=json.loads(receipt['stdout'])
    need(set(observed)=={'runtime','rows'} and set(observed['runtime'])=={'perl','carp','json_pp'}
         and all(type(v) is str and v for v in observed['runtime'].values()),'complete public runtime metadata')
    need([r['id'] for r in observed['rows']]==[r['id'] for r in plan['cases']],'complete ordered public regex corpus')
    lines=driver.decode().splitlines()
    called=next(i for i,line in enumerate(lines,1) if 'my $trace = emitter();' in line)
    caller=next(i for i,line in enumerate(lines,1) if 'my $row = displayed($regex);' in line)
    for case,row in zip(plan['cases'],observed['rows'],strict=True):
        need(set(row)=={'id','trace','value','profile','source_utf8'},'closed whole native regex observation')
        need(same(row['profile'],dict(**plan['profile'],MaxArgLen=case['limit'])),'actual complete selected regex profile')
        need(type(row['source_utf8']) is bool and row['source_utf8']==case['pattern_utf8'],'current selected constructor input encoding')
        expected=dict(kind='Regexp',codepoints=[ord(c) for c in case['body']],modifiers=case['modifiers'],
            pattern_utf8=case['pattern_utf8'],normalized='(?^'+case['modifiers']+':'+case['body']+')')
        need(same(row['value'],expected),'whole public compiled pattern/flags/encoding/normalized value')
        expected_trace=('regex source fixture at '+str(BASE/'native.pl')+' line '+str(called)+'.\n'
            '\tmain::displayed('+case['display']['token']+') called at '+str(BASE/'native.pl')+' line '+str(caller)+'\n')
        need(row['trace']==expected_trace,'whole source-generated regex public header and trace')
    # Actual paired construction intervention: unchanged characters, different
    # explicit input representation and resulting public modifiers/displays.
    for index in range(0,len(observed['rows']),9):
        literal,byte,wide=(observed['rows'][index+i] for i in (2,5,8))
        need(literal['value']==byte['value'] and byte['value']['codepoints']==wide['value']['codepoints']
             and byte['value']['modifiers']!=wide['value']['modifiers'], 'actual whole byte/upgraded construction separation')
    return dict(native=pin(receipt['stdout'].encode()),scope=SCOPE)

"""Execute the full inherited reader set and committed scalar qualification."""
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path
from common import AUTHORITY, BASE, CENSUS, SCALAR, REVISION, SCOPE, canonical, module, need, pin, save
from run import execute


def inputs():
    return [AUTHORITY, CENSUS/'census.json', CENSUS/'source-models.json',
            SCALAR/'manifest-qualified.json', SCALAR/'qualified-proof.json']


def readers():
    result = dict(module(Path('docs/audits/observer-predicate-values-20261010/common.py'))['READERS'])
    result['predicate-values'] = ['docs/audits/observer-predicate-values-20261010/verify.py']
    result['scalar-values'] = [str(SCALAR/'verify.py')]
    return result


def main():
    fixed = {}
    for path in inputs():
        command = ['git', '--no-replace-objects', 'show', REVISION+':'+str(path)]
        result = subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True)
        need(result.returncode == 0 and not result.stderr and result.stdout == path.read_bytes(),

    receipts = {name: execute('prerequisite-'+name, ['python3', '-B', *arguments])
                for name, arguments in readers().items()}

        readers={k:pin(canonical(v)) for k,v in receipts.items()}, scope=SCOPE))

    main()

"""Retain every actual command, stream and complete program epoch, including failures."""
import subprocess
import sys
from common import BASE, canonical, need, pin, save


def execute(label, command):
    previous = list(BASE.glob('actual-' + label + '-*.json'))
    name = 'actual-' + label + '-' + str(len(previous) + 1) + '.json'
    programs = {str(p):dict(identity=pin(p.read_bytes()), body=p.read_text())
                for p in sorted(BASE.iterdir()) if p.suffix in ('.py', '.pl')}
    result = subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True)
    record = dict(command=command, status=result.returncode, stdout=result.stdout,
                  stderr=result.stderr, programs=programs)
    save(name, record)
    print(name, result.returncode, result.stdout[-500:], result.stderr[-1000:], flush=True)
    need(type(result.returncode) is int and result.returncode == 0 and not result.stderr,
         'actual complete successful step: ' + name)
    return record


if __name__ == '__main__':
    need(len(sys.argv) >= 3, 'label and explicit command required')
    execute(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2:])

"""Authenticate the original child, ancestors and separately owned successor."""
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path
from common import BASE, REVISION, load, module, need, same, save

TASK=Path('docs/tasks/SEMANTIC-INTROSPECTION-MCP-FRONTIER.md')
prior=module(Path('docs/audits/observer-scalar-values-20261010/scope_verify.py'))


def derive():
    owner=(BASE/'scope.txt').read_text().splitlines()[0]
    remaining=owner.rsplit('.',1)[0]
    values=remaining.rsplit('.',1)[0]
    identifiers=[owner,remaining,values,values.rsplit('.',1)[0],remaining+'.1',remaining+'.3']
    command=['git','--no-replace-objects','show',REVISION+':'+str(TASK)]
    result=subprocess.run(command,capture_output=True,text=True)
    need(result.returncode==0 and not result.stderr,'whole original regex task source')
    bodies={identifier:prior['block'](result.stdout,identifier) for identifier in identifiers}
    current=TASK.read_text()
    for identifier,body in bodies.items():
        need(prior['contract'](prior['block'](current,identifier))==prior['contract'](body),
             'unchanged complete regex/remaining/value/header acceptance')
    return dict(revision=REVISION,task=str(TASK),original_bodies=bodies,
        scope='Only the regex child can close; original and ancestor acceptance and opaque boundaries retain.')


if __name__=='__main__':
    result=derive()
    if (BASE/'task-contracts.json').exists():
        need(same(result,load('task-contracts.json')),'whole immutable regex task contracts')
    else:
        save('task-contracts.json',result)
    print('PASS unchanged whole regex-child and ancestor/sibling contracts.')

"""Replay whole authored regex qualification with genuine independent controls."""
import base64
import copy
import gzip
import json
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path
from common import AUTHORITY, BASE, CENSUS, SCALAR, REVISION, SCOPE, canonical, load, need, pin, read, same, save
import derive
import oracle
import prerequisites
import scope_verify


def validation(product,plan,native):
    result=oracle.source(read(AUTHORITY),read(CENSUS/'source-models.json'),product,plan)
    need(native['command']==['perl','-Iperl',str(BASE/'native.pl')],'exact current regex public capture command')
    need(native['inputs']=={str(BASE/n):pin((BASE/n).read_bytes()) for n in ('native.pl','plan.json')},
         'whole selected regex driver/corpus capture identity')
    result['native']=oracle.native(plan,native,(BASE/'native.pl').read_bytes())
    return result


def falsify(product,plan,native):
    controls=[]
    def trial(name,mutation,cause):
        p,h,n=copy.deepcopy((product,plan,native))
        mutation(p,h,n)
        need(not same([p,h,n],[product,plan,native]),'genuine complete regex hostile candidate')
        try:
            validation(p,h,n)
        except ValueError as error:
            need(str(error)==cause,'intended regex rejection: '+name+': '+str(error))
            candidate=canonical(dict(product=p,plan=h,native=n))
            controls.append(dict(name=name,cause=cause,status='rejected',
                candidate_gzip_base64=base64.b64encode(gzip.compress(candidate,mtime=0)).decode()))
        else:
            raise ValueError('accepted hostile regex candidate: '+name)
    authored='whole independent authored regex expressions/flags/encoding'
    members='complete independent regex member/order/role/schema allocation'
    hypothesis='whole independent regex constructor/value/flags/encoding/display hypotheses'
    trial('changed-authored-expression',lambda p,h,n:p['authored'][0].update(expression='qr/borrowed/'),authored)
    trial('changed-whole-pattern',lambda p,h,n:p['authored'][0].update(body='borrowed'),authored)
    trial('invented-authored-modifier',lambda p,h,n:p['authored'][0].update(authored_modifiers='i'),authored)
    trial('invented-original-native-encoding',lambda p,h,n:p['authored'][0].update(original_native_flags_encoding='measured'),authored)
    trial('omitted-member',lambda p,h,n:p['members'].pop(),members)
    trial('reordered-members',lambda p,h,n:p['members'].reverse(),members)
    trial('borrowed-helper',lambda p,h,n:p['members'][0].update(helper=42),members)
    trial('wrong-role',lambda p,h,n:p['members'][0]['operand'].update(role='borrowed'),members)
    trial('extra-schema-field',lambda p,h,n:p['members'][0]['operand'].update(utf8=True),members)
    trial('original-native-promotion',lambda p,h,n:p.update(scope=SCOPE+' Original identity measured.'),'original versus current regex scope')
    trial('borrowed-profile',lambda p,h,n:h['profile'].update(MaxArgNums=8),'selected complete public profile')
    trial('wrong-selected-flag',lambda p,h,n:h['cases'][0].update(modifiers='i'),hypothesis)
    trial('wrong-selected-encoding',lambda p,h,n:h['cases'][0].update(pattern_utf8=True),hypothesis)
    trial('lost-pattern-tail',lambda p,h,n:h['cases'][0].update(body=h['cases'][0]['body'][:3]),hypothesis)
    trial('false-complete-prefix',lambda p,h,n:h['cases'][0]['display'].update(complete=True),hypothesis)
    def change(n,action):
        d=json.loads(n['stdout']); action(d); n['stdout']=canonical(d).decode()
    trial('boolean-status',lambda p,h,n:n.update(status=False),'actual typed public regex success')
    trial('omitted-native-case',lambda p,h,n:change(n,lambda d:d['rows'].pop()),'complete ordered public regex corpus')
    trial('native-borrowed-profile',lambda p,h,n:change(n,lambda d:d['rows'][0]['profile'].update(MaxArgLen=0)),
          'actual complete selected regex profile')
    trial('native-input-encoding',lambda p,h,n:change(n,lambda d:d['rows'][0].update(source_utf8=True)),
          'current selected constructor input encoding')
    trial('native-pattern-tail',lambda p,h,n:change(n,lambda d:d['rows'][0]['value']['codepoints'].append(88)),
          'whole public compiled pattern/flags/encoding/normalized value')
    trial('native-wrong-flags',lambda p,h,n:change(n,lambda d:d['rows'][0]['value'].update(modifiers='i')),
          'whole public compiled pattern/flags/encoding/normalized value')
    trial('native-wrong-pattern-encoding',lambda p,h,n:change(n,lambda d:d['rows'][0]['value'].update(pattern_utf8=True)),
          'whole public compiled pattern/flags/encoding/normalized value')
    trial('native-whole-trace',lambda p,h,n:change(n,lambda d:d['rows'][0].update(trace=d['rows'][0]['trace']+'borrowed\n')),
          'whole source-generated regex public header and trace')
    return controls


def main():
    need(same(scope_verify.derive(),load('task-contracts.json')),'complete unchanged task contracts')
    custody_command=['python3','-B',str(SCALAR/'verify.py')]
    custody=subprocess.run(custody_command,capture_output=True,text=True)
    need(type(custody.returncode) is int and custody.returncode==0 and custody.stderr=='' and custody.stdout.startswith('PASS '),
         'whole current committed scalar/source custody and replay')
    prior=load('prerequisites.json')
    need(prior['revision']==REVISION and prior['scope']==SCOPE and set(prior['fixed'])=={str(p) for p in prerequisites.inputs()},
         'complete fixed regex prerequisite domain')
    for path in prerequisites.inputs():
        command=['git','--no-replace-objects','show',REVISION+':'+str(path)]
        result=subprocess.run(command,capture_output=True)
        need(result.returncode==0 and not result.stderr and result.stdout==path.read_bytes()
             and prior['fixed'][str(path)]==dict(command=command,status=0,identity=pin(result.stdout)),
             'whole fixed/current regex input identity')
    readers=prerequisites.readers()
    need(set(prior['readers'])==set(readers),'whole prerequisite reader population')
    for name,arguments in readers.items():
        actual=load('actual-prerequisite-'+name+'-1.json')
        need(actual['command']==['python3','-B',*arguments] and type(actual['status']) is int and actual['status']==0
             and actual['stderr']=='' and 'PASS ' in actual['stdout'] and prior['readers'][name]==pin(canonical(actual)),
             'complete actual fresh prerequisite execution')
    product,plan,native=load('regexes.json'),load('plan.json'),load('native.json')
    need(same(derive.collect(read(AUTHORITY),read(CENSUS/'census.json'),read(CENSUS/'source-models.json')),product)
         and same(derive.plan(product),plan),'entire source product and selected corpus rederive')
    result=validation(product,plan,native)
    need(same({k:v for k,v in result.items() if k!='native'},load('source-proof.json')),'entire independent pre-observation proof')
    need(same(result['native'],load('native-proof.json')),'whole separate current regex proof')
    pre=load('pre-observation.json')
    need(pre['native_present'] is False and pre['scope']==SCOPE,'whole source-first hypothesis scope')
    selection=load('actual-source-selection-2.json')
    need(type(selection['status']) is int and selection['status']==0 and selection['stderr']=='','actual corrected source selection success')
    for name,identity in pre['inputs'].items():
        raw=selection['programs'][name]['body'].encode() if name in selection['programs'] else Path(name).read_bytes()
        need(pin(raw)==identity,'whole source-first program/input epoch')
    history=load('actual-root-history-1.json')
    need(history['command']==['git','--no-pager','log','-1','-S','regex_constructor_flags_encoding','--',str(CENSUS/'model.py')]
         and history['status']==0 and type(history['status']) is int and history['stderr']==''
         and history['stdout'].startswith('commit 6715ce66cf7b8a63c3a7f3125d722b578b29ad87\n'),'actual original regex-obligation history')
    controls=falsify(product,plan,native)
    need(same(controls,load('controls.json')),'whole independently replayed genuine regex controls')
    for path in BASE.glob('actual-*.json'):
        record=read(path)
        need(type(record['status']) is int and type(record['stdout']) is str and type(record['stderr']) is str,
             'complete typed actual result including first failures')
        for program in record['programs'].values():
            need(pin(program['body'].encode())==program['identity'],'whole actual program epoch')
    failed=load('actual-source-selection-1.json')
    need(failed['status']!=0 and 'finite authored ASCII pattern alphabet and absent modifiers' in failed['stderr'],
         'retained first finite source alphabet rejection')
    if (BASE/'manifest.json').exists():
        need(load('manifest.json')=={str(p.relative_to(BASE)):pin(p.read_bytes()) for p in BASE.rglob('*')
             if p.is_file() and p.name not in ('manifest.json','checks.json')},'whole immutable regex qualification namespace')
    proof=dict(result=result,controls=pin(canonical(controls)),scope=SCOPE,custody=dict(command=custody_command,
        status=custody.returncode,stdout=custody.stdout,stderr=custody.stderr,program=pin((SCALAR/'verify.py').read_bytes())))
    if (BASE/'proof.json').exists():
        need(same(proof,load('proof.json')),'whole immutable regex qualification proof')
    else:
        save('proof.json',proof)
    print('PASS whole authored regex expressions/source allocations, independent public constructors/flags/encoding/headers and genuine controls; original native identity/settings and parent scopes retain.')

=head1 NAME

re - Perl pragma to alter regular expression behaviour

=head1 SYNOPSIS

    use re 'taint';
    ($x) = ($^X =~ /^(.*)$/s);     # $x is tainted here

    $pat = '(?{ $foo = 1 })';
    use re 'eval';
    /foo${pat}bar/;		   # won't fail (when not under -T
                                   # switch)

    {
	no re 'taint';		   # the default
	($x) = ($^X =~ /^(.*)$/s); # $x is not tainted here

	no re 'eval';		   # the default
	/foo${pat}bar/;		   # disallowed (with or without -T
                                   # switch)
    }

    use re 'strict';               # Raise warnings for more conditions

    use re '/ix';
    "FOO" =~ / foo /; # /ix implied
    no re '/x';
    "FOO" =~ /foo/; # just /i implied

    use re 'debug';		   # output debugging info during
    /^(.*)$/s;			   # compile and run time


    use re 'debugcolor';	   # same as 'debug', but with colored
                                   # output
    ...

    use re qw(Debug All);          # Same as "use re 'debug'", but you
                                   # can use "Debug" with things other
                                   # than 'All'
    use re qw(Debug More);         # 'All' plus output more details
    no re qw(Debug ALL);           # Turn on (almost) all re debugging
                                   # in this scope

    use re qw(is_regexp regexp_pattern); # import utility functions
    my ($pat,$mods)=regexp_pattern(qr/foo/i);
    if (is_regexp($obj)) {
        print "Got regexp: ",
            scalar regexp_pattern($obj); # just as perl would stringify
    }                                    # it but no hassle with blessed
                                         # re's.

(We use $^X in these examples because it's tainted by default.)

=head1 DESCRIPTION

=head2 'taint' mode

When C<use re 'taint'> is in effect, and a tainted string is the target
of a regexp, the regexp memories (or values returned by the m// operator
in list context) are tainted.  This feature is useful when regexp operations
on tainted data aren't meant to extract safe substrings, but to perform
other transformations.

=head2 'eval' mode

When C<use re 'eval'> is in effect, a regexp is allowed to contain
C<(?{ ... })> zero-width assertions and C<(??{ ... })> postponed
subexpressions that are derived from variable interpolation, rather than
appearing literally within the regexp.  That is normally disallowed, since
it is a
potential security risk.  Note that this pragma is ignored when the regular
expression is obtained from tainted data, i.e.  evaluation is always
disallowed with tainted regular expressions.  See L<perlre/(?{ code })> 
and L<perlre/(??{ code })>.

For the purpose of this pragma, interpolation of precompiled regular
expressions (i.e., the result of C<qr//>) is I<not> considered variable
interpolation.  Thus:

    /foo${pat}bar/

I<is> allowed if $pat is a precompiled regular expression, even
if $pat contains C<(?{ ... })> assertions or C<(??{ ... })> subexpressions.

=head2 'strict' mode

Note that this is an experimental feature which may be changed or removed in a
future Perl release.

When C<use re 'strict'> is in effect, stricter checks are applied than
otherwise when compiling regular expressions patterns.  These may cause more
warnings to be raised than otherwise, and more things to be fatal instead of
just warnings.  The purpose of this is to find and report at compile time some
things, which may be legal, but have a reasonable possibility of not being the
programmer's actual intent.  This automatically turns on the C<"regexp">
warnings category (if not already on) within its scope.

As an example of something that is caught under C<"strict'>, but not
otherwise, is the pattern

 qr/\xABC/

The C<"\x"> construct without curly braces should be followed by exactly two
hex digits; this one is followed by three.  This currently evaluates as
equivalent to

 qr/\x{AB}C/

that is, the character whose code point value is C<0xAB>, followed by the
letter C<C>.  But since C<C> is a hex digit, there is a reasonable chance
that the intent was

 qr/\x{ABC}/

that is the single character at C<0xABC>.  Under C<'strict'> it is an error to
not follow C<\x> with exactly two hex digits.  When not under C<'strict'> a
warning is generated if there is only one hex digit, and no warning is raised
if there are more than two.

It is expected that what exactly C<'strict'> does will evolve over time as we
gain experience with it.  This means that programs that compile under it in
today's Perl may not compile, or may have more or fewer warnings, in future
Perls.  There is no backwards compatibility promises with regards to it.  Also
there are already proposals for an alternate syntax for enabling it.  For
these reasons, using it will raise a C<experimental::re_strict> class warning,
unless that category is turned off.

Note that if a pattern compiled within C<'strict'> is recompiled, say by
interpolating into another pattern, outside of C<'strict'>, it is not checked
again for strictness.  This is because if it works under strict it must work
under non-strict.

=head2 '/flags' mode

When C<use re '/I<flags>'> is specified, the given I<flags> are automatically
added to every regular expression till the end of the lexical scope.
I<flags> can be any combination of
C<'a'>,
C<'aa'>,
C<'d'>,
C<'i'>,
C<'l'>,
C<'m'>,
C<'n'>,
C<'p'>,
C<'s'>,
C<'u'>,
C<'x'>,
and/or
C<'xx'>.

C<no re '/I<flags>'> will turn off the effect of C<use re '/I<flags>'> for the
given flags.

For example, if you want all your regular expressions to have /msxx on by
default, simply put

    use re '/msxx';

at the top of your code.

The character set C</adul> flags cancel each other out. So, in this example,

    use re "/u";
    "ss" =~ /\xdf/;
    use re "/d";
    "ss" =~ /\xdf/;

the second C<use re> does an implicit C<no re '/u'>.

Similarly,

    use re "/xx";   # Doubled-x
    ...
    use re "/x";    # Single x from here on
    ...

Turning on one of the character set flags with C<use re> takes precedence over the
C<locale> pragma and the 'unicode_strings' C<feature>, for regular
expressions. Turning off one of these flags when it is active reverts to
the behaviour specified by whatever other pragmata are in scope. For
example:

    use feature "unicode_strings";
    no re "/u"; # does nothing
    use re "/l";
    no re "/l"; # reverts to unicode_strings behaviour

=head2 'debug' mode

When C<use re 'debug'> is in effect, perl emits debugging messages when
compiling and using regular expressions.  The output is the same as that
obtained by running a C<-DDEBUGGING>-enabled perl interpreter with the
B<-Dr> switch. It may be quite voluminous depending on the complexity
of the match.  Using C<debugcolor> instead of C<debug> enables a
form of output that can be used to get a colorful display on terminals
that understand termcap color sequences.  Set C<$ENV{PERL_RE_TC}> to a
comma-separated list of C<termcap> properties to use for highlighting
strings on/off, pre-point part on/off.
See L<perldebug/"Debugging Regular Expressions"> for additional info.

As of 5.9.5 the directive C<use re 'debug'> and its equivalents are
lexically scoped, as the other directives are.  However they have both
compile-time and run-time effects.

See L<perlmodlib/Pragmatic Modules>.

=head2 'Debug' mode

Similarly C<use re 'Debug'> produces debugging output, the difference
being that it allows the fine tuning of what debugging output will be
emitted. Options are divided into three groups, those related to
compilation, those related to execution and those related to special
purposes. The options are as follows:

=over 4

=item Compile related options

=over 4

=item COMPILE

Turns on all non-extra compile related debug options.

=item PARSE

Turns on debug output related to the process of parsing the pattern.

=item OPTIMISE

Enables output related to the optimisation phase of compilation.

=item TRIEC

Detailed info about trie compilation.

=item DUMP

Dump the final program out after it is compiled and optimised.

=item FLAGS

Dump the flags associated with the program

=item TEST

Print output intended for testing the internals of the compile process

=back

=item Execute related options

=over 4

=item EXECUTE

Turns on all non-extra execute related debug options.

=item MATCH

Turns on debugging of the main matching loop.

=item TRIEE

Extra debugging of how tries execute.

=item INTUIT

Enable debugging of start-point optimisations.

=back

=item Extra debugging options

=over 4

=item EXTRA

Turns on all "extra" debugging options.

=item BUFFERS

Enable debugging the capture group storage during match. Warning,
this can potentially produce extremely large output.

=item TRIEM

Enable enhanced TRIE debugging. Enhances both TRIEE
and TRIEC.

=item STATE

Enable debugging of states in the engine.

=item STACK

Enable debugging of the recursion stack in the engine. Enabling
or disabling this option automatically does the same for debugging
states as well. This output from this can be quite large.

=item GPOS

Enable debugging of the \G modifier.

=item OPTIMISEM

Enable enhanced optimisation debugging and start-point optimisations.
Probably not useful except when debugging the regexp engine itself.

=item OFFSETS

Dump offset information. This can be used to see how regops correlate
to the pattern. Output format is

   NODENUM:POSITION[LENGTH]

Where 1 is the position of the first char in the string. Note that position
can be 0, or larger than the actual length of the pattern, likewise length
can be zero.

=item OFFSETSDBG

Enable debugging of offsets information. This emits copious
amounts of trace information and doesn't mesh well with other
debug options.

Almost definitely only useful to people hacking
on the offsets part of the debug engine.

=item DUMP_PRE_OPTIMIZE

Enable the dumping of the compiled pattern before the optimization phase.

=item WILDCARD

When Perl encounters a wildcard subpattern, (see L<perlunicode/Wildcards in
Property Values>), it suspends compilation of the main pattern, compiles the
subpattern, and then matches that against all legal possibilities to determine
the actual code points the subpattern matches.  After that it adds these to
the main pattern, and continues its compilation.

You may very well want to see how your subpattern gets compiled, but it is
likely of less use to you to see how Perl matches that against all the legal
possibilities, as that is under control of Perl, not you.   Therefore, the
debugging information of the compilation portion is as specified by the other
options, but the debugging output of the matching portion is normally
suppressed.

You can use the WILDCARD option to enable the debugging output of this
subpattern matching.  Careful!  This can lead to voluminous outputs, and it
may not make much sense to you what and why Perl is doing what it is.
But it may be helpful to you to see why things aren't going the way you
expect.

Note that this option alone doesn't cause any debugging information to be
output.  What it does is stop the normal suppression of execution-related
debugging information during the matching portion of the compilation of
wildcards.  You also have to specify which execution debugging information you
want, such as by also including the EXECUTE option.

=back

=item Other useful flags

These are useful shortcuts to save on the typing.

=over 4

=item ALL

Enable all options at once except OFFSETS, OFFSETSDBG, BUFFERS, WILDCARD, and
DUMP_PRE_OPTIMIZE.
(To get every single option without exception, use both ALL and EXTRA, or
starting in 5.30 on a C<-DDEBUGGING>-enabled perl interpreter, use
the B<-Drv> command-line switches.)

=item All

Enable DUMP and all non-extra execute options. Equivalent to:

  use re 'debug';

=item MORE

=item More

Enable the options enabled by "All", plus STATE, TRIEC, and TRIEM.

=back

=back

As of 5.9.5 the directive C<use re 'debug'> and its equivalents are
lexically scoped, as are the other directives.  However they have both
compile-time and run-time effects.

=head2 Exportable Functions

As of perl 5.9.5 're' debug contains a number of utility functions that
may be optionally exported into the caller's namespace. They are listed
below.

=over 4

=item is_regexp($ref)

Returns true if the argument is a compiled regular expression as returned
by C<qr//>, false if it is not.

This function will not be confused by overloading or blessing. In
internals terms, this extracts the regexp pointer out of the
PERL_MAGIC_qr structure so it cannot be fooled.

=item regexp_pattern($ref)

If the argument is a compiled regular expression as returned by C<qr//>,
then this function returns the pattern.

In list context it returns a two element list, the first element
containing the pattern and the second containing the modifiers used when
the pattern was compiled.

  my ($pat, $mods) = regexp_pattern($ref);

In scalar context it returns the same as perl would when stringifying a raw
C<qr//> with the same pattern inside.  If the argument is not a compiled
reference then this routine returns false but defined in scalar context,
and the empty list in list context. Thus the following

    if (regexp_pattern($ref) eq '(?^i:foo)')

will be warning free regardless of what $ref actually is.

Like C<is_regexp> this function will not be confused by overloading
or blessing of the object.

=item regname($name,$all)

Returns the contents of a named buffer of the last successful match. If
$all is true, then returns an array ref containing one entry per buffer,
otherwise returns the first defined buffer.

=item regnames($all)

Returns a list of all of the named buffers defined in the last successful
match. If $all is true, then it returns all names defined, if not it returns
only names which were involved in the match.

=item regnames_count()

Returns the number of distinct names defined in the pattern used
for the last successful match.

B<Note:> this result is always the actual number of distinct
named buffers defined, it may not actually match that which is
returned by C<regnames()> and related routines when those routines
have not been called with the $all parameter set.

=item regmust($ref)

If the argument is a compiled regular expression as returned by C<qr//>,
then this function returns what the optimiser considers to be the longest
anchored fixed string and longest floating fixed string in the pattern.

A I<fixed string> is defined as being a substring that must appear for the
pattern to match. An I<anchored fixed string> is a fixed string that must
appear at a particular offset from the beginning of the match. A I<floating
fixed string> is defined as a fixed string that can appear at any point in
a range of positions relative to the start of the match. For example,

    my $qr = qr/here .* there/x;
    my ($anchored, $floating) = regmust($qr);
    print "anchored:'$anchored'\nfloating:'$floating'\n";

results in

    anchored:'here'
    floating:'there'

Because the C<here> is before the C<.*> in the pattern, its position
can be determined exactly. That's not true, however, for the C<there>;
it could appear at any point after where the anchored string appeared.
Perl uses both for its optimisations, preferring the longer, or, if they are
equal, the floating.

B<NOTE:> This may not necessarily be the definitive longest anchored and
floating string. This will be what the optimiser of the Perl that you
are using thinks is the longest. If you believe that the result is wrong
please report it via the L<perlbug> utility.

=item optimization($ref)

If the argument is a compiled regular expression as returned by C<qr//>,
then this function returns a hashref of the optimization information
discovered at compile time, so we can write tests around it. If any
other argument is given, returns C<undef>.

The hash contents are expected to change from time to time as we develop
new ways to optimize - no assumption of stability should be made, not
even between minor versions of perl.

For the current version, the hash will have the following contents:

=over 4

=item minlen

An integer, the least number of characters in any string that can match.

=item minlenret

An integer, the least number of characters that can be in C<$&> after a
match. (Consider eg C< /ns(?=\d)/ >.)

=item gofs

An integer, the number of characters before C<pos()> to start match at.

=item noscan

A boolean, C<TRUE> to indicate that any anchored/floating substrings
found should not be used. (CHECKME: apparently this is set for an
anchored pattern with no floating substring, but never used.)

=item isall

A boolean, C<TRUE> to indicate that the optimizer information is all
that the regular expression contains, and thus one does not need to
enter the regexp runtime engine at all.

=item anchor SBOL

A boolean, C<TRUE> if the pattern is anchored to start of string.

=item anchor MBOL

A boolean, C<TRUE> if the pattern is anchored to any start of line
within the string.

=item anchor GPOS

A boolean, C<TRUE> if the pattern is anchored to the end of the previous
match.

=item skip

A boolean, C<TRUE> if the start class can match only the first of a run.

=item implicit

A boolean, C<TRUE> if a C</.*/> has been turned implicitly into a C</^.*/>.

=item anchored/floating

A byte string representing an anchored or floating substring respectively
that any match must contain, or undef if no such substring was found, or
if the substring would require utf8 to represent.

=item anchored utf8/floating utf8

A utf8 string representing an anchored or floating substring respectively
that any match must contain, or undef if no such substring was found, or
if the substring contains only 7-bit ASCII characters.

=item anchored min offset/floating min offset

An integer, the first offset in characters from a match location at which
we should look for the corresponding substring.

=item anchored max offset/floating max offset

An integer, the last offset in characters from a match location at which
we should look for the corresponding substring.

Ignored for anchored, so may be 0 or same as min.

=item anchored end shift/floating end shift

FIXME: not sure what this is, something to do with lookbehind. regcomp.c
says:
    When the final pattern is compiled and the data is moved from the
    scan_data_t structure into the regexp structure the information
    about lookbehind is factored in, with the information that would
    have been lost precalculated in the end_shift field for the
    associated string.

=item checking

A constant string, one of "anchored", "floating" or "none" to indicate
which substring (if any) should be checked for first.

=item stclass

A string representation of a character class ("start class") that must
be the first character of any match.

TODO: explain the representations.

=back

=back

=head1 SEE ALSO

L<perlmodlib/Pragmatic Modules>.
